title: Senior asks: a client sends the JSON {"a":1,"a":2} to write(). What do you get after json_decode()?
explain: PHP does not reject duplicate keys. The last value wins, and the first one is lost without any error. JSON itself does not forbid it. If it matters, check the raw text or tell the client that keys must be unique.

title: PHP 8. The key exists, but the value is null. What does this print?
explain: isset() is false for null, even if the key exists. array_key_exists() only checks the key. Use it when null is a real value, for example a CSV cell that is empty on purpose.

title: What does Node print (a normal .js file, no strict mode)?
explain: o.g() has o before the dot, so this is o. (0, o.g)() is a plain function call, so this is the global object, which has no n. Same bug as a method passed as a callback: use an arrow function or bind().
